title: Entropy-weighted slice prioritizer for CI perf gating
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Our current CI perf gate runs a fixed set of slices for PRs which often misses regressions that appear in low-frequency or high-variance workload slices. This leads to noisy alerts and occasional production regressions. Goal: implement an entropy-weighted slice prioritizer that dynamically ranks candidate slices for PR-level microbench runs. The prioritizer should blend historical variance (p95 volatility), recent drift signals, and synthetic uncertainty (active probe results) to pick the smallest set of slices that maximizes detection power while keeping CI cost under the PR budget. The feature will be integrated into the existing PR perf harness and baseline reconciler so that every PR run chooses ~6 prioritized slices by default and falls back to the canonical baseline when required.
acceptance_criteria: PR-level run chooses prioritized slices within budget (<= 8 microbench slices) for 95% of PRs
Detection sensitivity: at least 85% detection rate on our synthetic regression corpus for p95 increases >= 6% or tokens/sec drops >= 8%
False positive rate under historical noise < 3% (measured over last 90 days sample)
Integration: prioritized selection returns slice IDs to CI runner and is recorded in perf run metadata (dashboard and traces)
Operational: alerts generated by gating rules reference the slice priority score and sample trace links
technical_notes: Score components: entropy(history) = H(p95 distribution across last N runs), volatility = rolling std of p95, recent_drift = exponentially-weighted mean of delta to baseline, active_probe_uncertainty = probe variance from 10 synthetic microburst injections

Ranking formula (prototype): score = w1*normalized_entropy + w2*normalized_volatility + w3*abs(recent_drift) + w4*probe_uncertainty. Initial weights w1..w4 = [0.35, 0.25, 0.25, 0.15], tuned post-launch
Stat testing: use Bayesian sequential testing for early stop and false-positive control; fall back to Mann-Whitney U for nonparametric confirmation when sample sizes small
Budgeting: convert slice cost to "tokens-equivalent" using historical avg tokens/sec * runtime. Ensure sum(costs) <= PR_budget_tokens (~3e8 tokens equivalent currently)
Data: leverages perf-history index (Influx/Grafana) + run fingerprints from baseline reconciler to compute entropy. Maintain a 90-day sliding window by default
Compatibility: must work with both hosted and dedicated CI runners; selection logic runs in ci-selector microservice with TTL cache for slice metadata
Metrics to emit: selected_slice_count, selection_time_ms, score_breakdown (list of top-6 scores), detection_outcome, bayes_evidence_ratio
implementation_plan: Spike (3d): implement prototype selector in python using historical perf dumps -> validate on synthetic corpus (Ravi)
API: add /select-slices endpoint returning ordered slice IDs + score vector (ci-selector team)
CI integration: modify pr-perf-runner to call selector and run only returned slices; add feature flag 'entropy-slice-selector'
Dashboard: add Grafana panel showing selected slices and score components per PR run (observability)
Tune: run canary on 10% of PRs for 2 weeks, gather detection/FP metrics, adjust weights and thresholds
Docs: write Confluence playbook + examples and update perf-runner README
Rollout: enable for all PRs after canary if detection metrics meet ACs
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring logic and normalization (CI)
Synthetic regression corpus: inject 200 synthetic regressions across rare slices with controlled p95/tokens/sec deltas; measure detection rate
A/B canary: compare current fixed-slice gate vs entropy-prioritized selection on 1k PRs to measure FP and detection improvement
Load test: ensure selector responds < 200ms under 200 RPS (cache warm) and < 500ms cold
Backward compatibility tests: ensure baseline reconciler still produces canonical baseline and selector falls back when history insufficient
Chaos: simulate missing perf-history data and verify graceful fallback to size-based sampling
